# Ryu scientific-notation binary64 formatting: known answers, upstream's suite.
#
# Provenance
#   Every expected string below is the literal upstream asserts, copied from
#   the gtest cases of `EXPECT_EXP(value, precision, expected)` in
#   ryu/ryu/tests/d2fixed_test.cc at the pinned upstream revision
#   4c0618b0e44f7ef027ebae05d2cc7812048f7c8f.  Nothing in this file was
#   computed by this fork.  Upstream's two generated tables
#   (all_powers_of_ten, all_binary_exponents) are not copied whole; the
#   hand-written cases upstream names one by one are, including the 750-digit
#   one, plus the single longest entry of the first table - see the note at
#   the end of this header.
#
# Line format
#   <input-spec> TAB <precision> TAB <expected string>
#
#   input-spec is one of
#     zero          upstream's literal 0.0
#     bits   <16 hex digits>
#                   upstream's int64Bits2Double(0x...) helper
#     parts  <sign 0|1> <exponent> <mantissa>
#                   upstream's ieeeParts2Double(sign, exponent, mantissa);
#                   the mantissa keeps the literal base upstream wrote it in
#     lit    <decimal literal>
#                   the upstream C literal
#
#   Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.
#
# One row is not from a hand-written case: `lit 1e-323` at precision 749 is
# `all_powers_of_ten[0]`'s scientific answer, which upstream checks through
# `D2expTest.AllPowersOfTen`.  It is here as the longest scientific answer
# upstream states.  The rest of that table is generated and is not copied.
#
# The exponent marker is upstream's and differs from the shortest form on
# purpose: lowercase `e`, an explicit `+` for a nonnegative exponent, and at
# least two exponent digits (`1.25e+00`, `1e+54`, `4.940656...e-324`).  That
# spelling is part of the known answers and is not normalised anywhere.
